accepted_for: Internal cold-core production shell with a small, conspicuous seam defect.
original_quote: The seam on that cold core print that just finished did not turn out great. I mean, if this were an exterior surface, we'd have to keep iterating for a while. I mean, it's fine and it's probably better than the seam that we had before that was protruding more, but I don't think the scarf is helping anything there, as you can see in the photos. I guess it's fine to leave this as our production settings for production print. This will work, but just make a note of the pretty obvious visual defect we have there. I don't see any reason that this would be a structural defect, though. Everything seems solid enough, and I don't think this is going to interfere with assembly in any way. It's really quite small, just very noticeable. So please make a note of all of that and call it a success, as far as such things go.

production_settings.disposition: Retain current production settings, including the A2 scarf treatment.

visual_assessment.defect: Small but very noticeable seam line and local surface irregularity.
visual_assessment.scarf: Derek sees no apparent cosmetic benefit from the scarf.
visual_assessment.exterior_surface: An exterior show surface with this finish would need further iteration.

structural_assessment: Derek reports that everything seems solid enough and sees no reason to regard the seam as a structural defect.
assembly_assessment: Derek expects the small seam defect not to interfere with assembly.
scope: Derek's visual and hands-on assessment of this completed shell; assembly fit is an expectation in his report.
